ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher; no account flag (the driver was stationary at the pickup, so no abuse-of-button finding) — record the procedural lapse that no "I'm Here" tap was made.
ruling.reasoning:
Cancellation entry: NS-0, driver-cancelled with a claimed no-show → NS-1/NS-2. NS-1 requires (i) the driver to have pressed "I'm Here" (or platform auto-arrival), (ii) GPS at the pickup point at that moment, and (iii) a continuous wait of >3 minutes within 200 m after the tap. The record shows driver_pressed_here_at = null, arrival_confirmed_by = null, arrival_radius_m = null, wait_started_at = null, wait_expired_at = null — requirement (i) is not met. The driver's own statement confirms this: "I forgot to press the I'm Here button." Under NS-2, failure of any of (i)(ii)(iii) → the $6.61 cancellation fee is refunded in full (refund_full).

Independent GPS arithmetic corroborates: at the driver's message "At the pickup point" (22:43:20) the trace is at (1.436022, 103.78615), ~33 m from the pickup (1.436, 103.7865) — he was physically at the pickup, and he then stayed essentially stationary through the 22:46:50 cancel timestamp (~4 min 20 s), so I do not treat the wait-length element as contrived. But NS-1 is conjunctive: a tap (or a platform auto-arrival confirmation) is required and none is recorded. Note the rider's complaint ("on my way down") is not a defence the driver can invoke; it is simply the explanation the platform is meant to test via the button protocol, which was not followed.

No evidence gap: the GPS trace is dense (5 s grid, thinned to 30 s) and covers the whole window, arrival to cancellation, so nothing needs to be presumed either way (contrast NS-1's断档/coverage rule). No account flag: the flag in NS-2 attaches only when the driver pressed "I'm Here" while GPS showed him outside the pickup radius (>200 m); here no tap occurred and the GPS shows him at the pickup, so no abuse of the cancellation/waiting button. Profile facts (driver no_show_disputes_upheld_90d = 0) are not used to decide anything.

Safety screen: the chat is a pickup arrangement plus a cancellation notice; the complaint and driver statement contain no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation. safety_concern = none.

Non-metered (RydeX) fixed fare, so the only disputed item is the cancellation fee; amount = $6.61, paid as a Ryde voucher per NS-7.

rejected_claims.reason: The driver's claim that he waited 4 minutes at the pickup is not disputed on the GPS (he was stationary there from ~22:43 to the 22:46:50 cancellation), but NS-1 is conjunctive: without an 'I'm Here' tap or platform auto-arrival confirmation the no-show fee cannot stand, and he admits he did not press the button.
The rider's 'I was on my way down' does not by itself excuse lateness, but it is irrelevant here — the fee fails on the driver-side NS-1 requirements, not on the rider's timing.
